Super Superstition (Song About A Post in /v/TheDinnerTable)

I'm a very broke university student but I still try to keep my diet reasonably healthy. For dinner I usually just eat some rice and a lot of roasted vegetables, which I don't think I'd be able to do every day without smothering it in this gravy, so I thought I might share it in case someone else might like to start making their rice and veggies more palatable! I don't think it's very costly and the recipe yields a considerable amount of gravy (I store it in the fridge for about a week before it's finished, so I can't claim that it lasts longer than that).

Ingredients:

  • 1 tablespoon oil (I use olive, sunflower or canola, whatever's typically at hand in my kitchen)

  • 1/4 onion (finely chopped)

  • 2 garlic cloves (finely chopped)

  • 1 tablespoon tomato paste

  • Splash of white wine (I guess a quarter cup?)

  • 1 litre vegetable stock (I'm a vegetarian, but I'm sure you could use chicken stock. Might even be nicer!)

  • 1 tablespoon mustard powder

  • 1 tablespoon Marmite

Method:

  • Saute' the onion on medium-high heat in a medium-big saucepan until good and glassy.

  • Add the minced garlic and tomato paste and saute' for about a minute.

  • Splash some white wine in and saute' for half a minute.

  • Add the stock, mustard powder and Marmite.

  • Bring to boil, then lower the heat to medium-low and reduce to half before eating.

I apologise for all this text, I know it's preferred to simply post a link to a nice recipe, but this gravy really has helped me improve my heating habits (it makes roasted Brussels sprouts quite tasty) and I thought other people might appreciate it. I hope you like it!
